notes_list.title: Reducing Agents — LiAlH4 and NaBH4
notes_list.basic_overview: LiAlH4 is a strong hydride donor capable of reducing many carbonyl derivatives; NaBH4 is milder and often selectively reduces aldehydes and ketones.
notes_list.extra_info_content: LiAlH4 commonly reduces esters, acids, amides and nitriles under suitable conditions; NaBH4 is typically milder and compatible with many other functional groups.
notes_list.examples: RCHO/R2CO → alcohols; ester → primary alcohol with LiAlH4; carboxylic acid → primary alcohol with LiAlH4 after workup.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: LiAlH4 reacts violently with protic solvents and is used in dry ether/THF followed by careful aqueous workup. NaBH4 is compatible with protic solvents in many applications.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Hydride attacks electrophilic carbonyl carbon, producing tetrahedral intermediates. Carbonyl derivatives can undergo acyl substitution before further reduction.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Hydride-transfer kinetics depend on carbonyl electrophilicity and reagent/solvent environment.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not add LiAlH4 directly to water/alcohol. Always distinguish chemoselectivity of LiAlH4 vs NaBH4.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
